about: ACDC scenarios for step 6 of the decision procedure (docs/design.md, ACDC, Edges): each edge in the provenance DAG graded on its own checks, with the I2I operator named explicitly.

cases.title: Chained ACDC, I2I edge valid
cases.description: The presented ACDC has an edge with the I2I operator and the S1 schema to a far node issued by another identifier to the presented ACDC's issuer. Every node is sealed by its issuer. A validator should find the ACDC and the edge valid.

cases.title: I2I edge to a far node targeted at someone else
cases.description: As KS-39, but the far node's issuee is not the near node's issuer, which the I2I operator requires (line 1205).

companion.title: I2I edge to a far node targeted at someone else: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-40, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Far node changed with its SAID left as the edge names
cases.description: The far node was issued to another party; its issuee was then rewritten to the near node's issuer and its attribute block's SAID recomputed, but its top-level SAID left equal to the edge's n. Recomputing the far node's SAID (line 1174) shows it is not the node the edge names.

companion.title: Far node changed with its SAID left as the edge names: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-41b, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Far node forged to point back at the near node
cases.description: As KS-49, but the bundle's middle node has its edge rewritten after its SAIDs were computed, keeping the length, to name the presented ACDC instead of the root, with its top-level SAID left equal to the edge's n. Read by their claimed SAIDs the two nodes form a cycle. Recomputing the middle node's SAID (line 1174) shows it is not the node the edge names, so a validator that recomputes before it follows the node's own edges never meets the cycle and refuses the edge; one that indexes far nodes by their claimed SAID and walks first may never answer, which fails every assertion. The case's dag lists the edges of the nodes as issued, which hold no cycle.

companion.title: Far node forged to point back at the near node: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-41c, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Edge schema satisfied
cases.description: As KS-39, but the edge names a stricter schema, S3, which requires a role attribute, and the far node has one. A validator should find the edge valid.

cases.title: Far node under a stricter schema of its own
cases.description: As KS-39, but the far node is issued under S3, which requires a role attribute, and has one, while the edge names the more lenient S1. The far node satisfies both its own schema and the edge's, so a validator should find the edge valid.

cases.title: Far node fails its own schema but satisfies the edge's
cases.description: As KS-42q, but the far node has no role attribute, so it fails its own schema, S3, while it satisfies the edge's, S1. Line 1174 requires the far node to satisfy its own schema, and line 1178 makes the edge's schema an additional constraint, so the edge is not valid. A validator that checks the far node only against the edge's schema when the edge names one accepts it.

companion.title: Far node fails its own schema but satisfies the edge's: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-42d, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Far node fails the edge's schema
cases.description: As KS-42p, but the far node has no role attribute. It satisfies its own schema, not the edge's (line 1178).

companion.title: Far node fails the edge's schema: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-42, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Edge schema absent
cases.description: As KS-42p, but the bundle does not hold the schema the edge names, so the far node cannot be confirmed to validate against it (line 1178).

companion.title: Edge schema absent: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-42b, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Edge schema substituted
cases.description: As KS-42b, but the bundle holds a lenient schema with a correct SAID of its own in place of the one the edge names, and the far node has no role. A schema whose SAID is not the edge's s does not stand in for it.

companion.title: Edge schema substituted: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-42c, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: I2I edge to an untargeted far node
cases.description: The edge names the I2I operator, but the far node, valid under its own schema, has no issuee. To be valid, the far node of an I2I edge must be targeted (line 1205).

companion.title: I2I edge to an untargeted far node: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-44, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Far node absent
cases.description: As KS-39, but the bundle does not hold the far node, so its SAID cannot be confirmed (line 1174).

companion.title: Far node absent: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-45, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Two-hop chain, valid
cases.description: The presented ACDC's edge points to a far node whose own edge points to a root ACDC; each edge uses I2I, and each node is sealed by its issuer. A validator should find both edges and the ACDC valid.

cases.title: Two-hop chain, the deeper edge fails I2I
cases.description: As KS-49, but the root ACDC is targeted at someone other than the middle node's issuer, so the deeper edge fails I2I (line 1205). The validator evaluates edges anywhere in the provenance DAG.

companion.title: Two-hop chain, the deeper edge fails I2I: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-50, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Diamond
cases.description: The presented ACDC has edges to two far nodes, each of which has an edge to one root ACDC. Each of the four edges is reported once, keyed by its near node, and all are valid.

cases.title: Diamond, the edge from F2 into the shared root fails I2I
cases.description: As KS-51, but F2 is issued by an identifier other than the root's issuee and sealed in that identifier's KEL, so its edge into the root fails I2I (line 1205) while F1's edge into the same root holds. The two edges share a far node and differ only in their near issuer, so a validator that treats I2I as a property of the far node, or caches an edge's result by the far node's SAID, reports one of them wrongly. Evaluated in delivery order, the failing edge is the second into the root; KS-53 is the mirror.

companion.title: Diamond, the edge from F2 into the shared root fails I2I: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-52, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.

cases.title: Diamond, the edge from F1 into the shared root fails I2I
cases.description: As KS-51, but F1 is issued by an identifier other than the root's issuee and sealed in that identifier's KEL, so its edge into the root fails I2I (line 1205) while F2's edge into the same root holds. The two edges share a far node and differ only in their near issuer, so a validator that treats I2I as a property of the far node, or caches an edge's result by the far node's SAID, reports one of them wrongly. Evaluated in delivery order, the failing edge is the first into the root; KS-52 is the mirror.

companion.title: Diamond, the edge from F1 into the shared root fails I2I: the edge
companion.description: The MUST half of KS-53, ungated: the failing edge, if reported, is not valid.
